title: 第十五章 人活一世草木一秋第十六章 长坂坡
slug: 民国戏子请叫我武道宗师
content_zh:
“上个屁！”
刘管事恼羞成怒，把气全撒在了掌柜身上。
“没看见人都走了吗，结账，挂我们庆和班的账上！”
说完，他拽着腿软的小盛云，逃也似的往外走，一刻也不敢多待。
等这帮瘟神走了，掌柜的这才松了口气，招呼伙计收拾残局。
“掌柜的，您快看。”
正在擦桌子的小伙计突然叫了一声，指着陆诚刚才坐过位置背后的那根楠木柱子。
“咋呼什么，没见过世面。”
掌柜的骂骂咧咧地走过去，顺着伙计的手指一瞧。
这一瞧，老掌柜的眼珠子定住了。
只见那根两人合抱粗，刷着朱红大漆的楠木柱子上，赫然钉着一片白色的瓷片。
那瓷片只有指甲盖大小，边缘锋利如刀。
最吓人的是，这并不是浅浅地插在表面。
它是“嵌”进去的。
入木三分！
只有一道细细的白线露在外面，周围的漆面竟然没有丝毫崩裂，就像是这瓷片本来就是长在木头里的一样。
“我的乖乖……”
掌柜的倒吸一口凉气，“这是刚才那位陆老板弄的？”
“可不是嘛，我刚才在门口偷瞧了一眼。”
小伙计咽了口唾沫，“就听见‘崩’的一声，比放炮仗还脆，然后就这样了。”

掌柜的伸手去摸，滑溜溜的，冰凉刺骨。
“拿钳子来。”
掌柜的来了劲头，“这可是好木头，别以后发霉烂了，得拔出来。”
伙计赶紧找来一把平日里起钉子的大铁钳。
掌柜的夹住那露出来的一丁点瓷片头，咬着牙，腮帮子鼓起，使出了吃奶的劲儿往外拔。
“嘿，我还不信了。”
纹丝不动。
那瓷片就像是在木头里生了根。
“让我来试试？”
就在掌柜的累得满头大汗的时候，身后传来一个苍老却中气十足的声音。
掌柜的一回头，赶紧把钳子放下，换上一副恭敬的神色。
“哟，五爷，您还没走呢？”
来人正是之前在德云茶园出现过的谭五爷，北平梨园行的泰斗，也是个真正懂功夫的行家。
谭五爷手里转着两颗玛瑙球，背着手走到柱子前，伸出那双有些枯瘦的手，摸了摸那道瓷片留下的痕迹。
良久。
五爷叹了口气，眼神复杂。
“别拔了。”
他转过身，看着掌柜的。
content_en:
"Fuck you!"
Manager Liu became so angry that he took all his anger on the shopkeeper.
"Didn't you see that everyone has left? Pay the bill and put it on the account of our Qinghe class!"
After saying that, he grabbed Xiao Shengyun, whose legs were weak, and ran out as if running away, not daring to stay for a moment longer.
After these plague gods left, the shopkeeper breathed a sigh of relief and called on his assistants to clean up the mess.
"Shopkeeper, look quickly."
The boy who was cleaning the table suddenly called out and pointed to the nanmu pillar behind the seat where Lu Cheng had just sat.
"What are you talking about? I have never seen the world."
Cursing, the shopkeeper walked over and took a look at the waiter's finger.
At this glance, the old shopkeeper's eyes froze.
I saw a piece of white porcelain nailed to the nanmu pillar that was as thick as two people's arms and painted with vermilion paint.
The porcelain piece was only the size of a fingernail, and its edge was as sharp as a knife.
The most frightening thing is that this is not a shallow insertion on the surface.
It is "embedded" in.
penetrating!
Only a thin white line was exposed, and the surrounding paint surface did not crack at all, as if the porcelain piece had originally grown in the wood.
"My dear..."
The shopkeeper took a deep breath, "Is this done by Boss Lu just now?"
"No, I just took a peek at the door."
The boy swallowed, "I heard a 'collapse', which was crisper than a firecracker, and then that was it."
The shopkeeper reached out to touch it and found it was slippery and cold to the bone.
"Get the pliers."
The shopkeeper got excited and said, "This is good wood. Don't let it get moldy and rotten in the future and you have to pull it out."
The boy quickly found a pair of large iron pliers that he usually used to pick up nails.
The shopkeeper clamped the exposed tip of the porcelain piece, gritted his teeth, puffed up his cheeks, and pulled it out with all his strength.
"Hey, I still don't believe it."
Not moving at all.
The porcelain pieces seemed to have roots in the wood.
"Let me try?"
Just when the shopkeeper was sweating profusely from exhaustion, an old but energetic voice came from behind.
When the shopkeeper turned around, he quickly put down the pliers and put on a respectful look.
"Hey, Fifth Master, you haven't left yet?"
The person who came was none other than Mr. Tan Wu who had appeared in Deyun Tea Garden before. He was a master of Peking Opera House and a real expert in kung fu.
Tan Wuye turned two agate balls in his hand, walked to the pillar with his hands behind his back, stretched out his somewhat skinny hands, and touched the traces left by the porcelain shards.
a long time.
Fifth Master sighed, his eyes complicated.
"Stop pulling it out."
He turned around and looked at the shopkeeper.
